title: A zero-knowledge proof of 3-coloring
sub: Convince someone a graph is 3-colorable without revealing how. The prover hides the coloring; the verifier opens one edge per round.

frames.caption: The prover claims to know a 3-coloring. Each round they shuffle the three colors, hide every vertex, and the verifier opens the two ends of one random edge.
Round 1: open edge D–E. Two different colors, as they should be. Because the colors were freshly shuffled, the verifier learns nothing else.

After 18 rounds a cheater would have slipped through with probability 12%. Run k·|E| rounds and that falls to about e<sup>−k</sup>, while the verifier has still only seen pairs of different, randomly named colors.

Round 5: open edge A–B. Same color! The coloring is invalid, and the verifier rejects.
